flagged.title: Context: The Gothic Tradition
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly tells students that AO4 tests context on this 40-mark Eduqas question, directly contradicting the syllabus and the lesson text which clarifies that AO4 is SPaG (accuracy of writing) and context is not an assessed objective.

mark_affecting.video_says: an absolutely crucial part of that wider text question is AO4, context.
mark_affecting.lesson_says: It rewards AO1 (a personal response supported by evidence), AO2 (language, form and structure) and AO4, which is the accuracy of your own writing. Context is not a marked objective here

flagged.title: Chapters 1-4: Arthur's Journey
flagged.reason: The video presents an inaccurate direct quotation on screen and in voiceover ('a wasted face... so that the bones of her face showed through') and describes the woman as 'veiled' rather than wearing a bonnet.

mark_affecting.quote: Arthur spots a veiled figure in deepest black... 'a wasted face... so that the bones of her face showed through.'

flagged.title: Chapters 5-8: Eel Marsh House
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly claims Arthur is inside the house and rushes outside when hearing the pony and trap, building extensive false analysis around sound penetrating the walls, which would penalise a student's AO1 textual knowledge.

mark_affecting.quote: Arthur is inside, trying to work, when this intense sensory attack begins... the sound literally penetrates the thick walls of Eel Marsh House... Arthur rushes outside to help

flagged.title: Atmosphere & Narrative Technique
flagged.reason: The video claims Arthur breaks down the nursery door, contradicting the lesson text and teaching a film-adaptation error that GCSE examiners explicitly penalise under AO1.

mark_affecting.video_says: while the locked nursery conceals its profound significance until Arthur is finally forced to break down the door
mark_affecting.lesson_says: the locked nursery conceals its significance until the door opens by itself

flagged.title: Symbolism & Setting
flagged.reason: The video presents the fabricated scene where Arthur discovers Nathaniel buried in a separate grave from the Drablow family plot, which would penalise students for textual inaccuracy under AO1.

mark_affecting.quote: what's crucial to notice here is that Nathaniel is buried totally separately from the main Drablow family plot... Nathaniel's separate grave reflects his status as an illegitimate child

flagged.title: Key Themes & Exam Technique
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly defines AO4 as context and instructs students to weave in context to earn AO4 marks, whereas in Eduqas GCSE English Literature context is not assessed on this text and AO4 exclusively assesses spelling, punctuation, and grammar.

mark_affecting.video_says: And hey, this is exactly where you can secure your AO4 context marks... naturally weaving in your AO4 context (also shown on screen at 06:34: 'Context (AO4)')
mark_affecting.lesson_says: You are marked on AO1 (a personal response supported by evidence), AO2 (language, form and structure) and AO4, the accuracy and control of your own writing. Context is not a marked objective, so there are no marks for a context paragraph.
